tasks.title: Add `intro` rich-text page property and emit it into OG/meta tags

finalDraft.title: Add `intro` rich-text page property and emit it into OG/meta tags
finalDraft.description:
Why: Decision #12 (single source of truth for intro): the `intro` page property must drive `<meta name="intro">`, `<meta property="og:description">`, and `<meta name="twitter:description">`. The same property will also drive the first body paragraph, but body rendering is owned by T-007/T-009 — this task is scoped to the property + meta emission only.

What:
1. Add an `./intro` rich-text granite field to the press-release page-properties dialog at `ui.apps/src/main/content/jcr_root/apps/<project>/components/page/press-release/_cq_dialog/.content.xml` (same file touched by T-002).
2. Emit `intro` into the three meta tags above from `ui.apps/src/main/content/jcr_root/apps/<project>/components/page/press-release/customheaderlibs.html`.
3. Strip HTML for meta-tag content using server-side Jsoup (`Jsoup.clean(value, Safelist.none())`) exposed via a Sling Model or Use-class — not HTL `@ context`, since meta `content=` requires plain text, not HTML-escaped markup.

Edge cases: when `intro` is empty/blank after stripping, the three meta tags MUST NOT be emitted at all (no empty `content=""`). Rich text remains intact in JCR for body rendering downstream.
acceptance_criteria: Given an editor sets `intro` to "Qantas Group today provided a market update.", when the page renders, then `<meta name="intro">`, `<meta property="og:description">`, and `<meta name="twitter:description">` are present and each `content` attribute equals the plain-text string exactly.
Given `intro` is empty or contains only whitespace/empty markup after HTML stripping, when the page renders, then none of the three meta tags are emitted in the response HTML.

Given `intro` contains `bold and italic`, when the page renders, then meta-tag `content` equals `bold and italic` (tags stripped) and the stored JCR property still contains the original rich-text markup for downstream body rendering.

Given `intro` contains characters requiring HTML attribute escaping (`"`, `&`, `<`), when the page renders, then meta-tag `content` is properly attribute-escaped and the page validates as well-formed HTML.

finalDraft.description:

- `jcr:content` (template metadata)
- `structure/` defining the locked regions: header XF placeholder, Article Header group placeholder, Layout Container (editable, body), Core List (Related Posts) placeholder, footer XF placeholder.
- `initial/` left empty (or with the body container only) — the structure provides the locked chrome.
- `policies/` skeleton (actual policies authored in T-018).
- `template-types/` registration if not already present.

Mark the regions per the component tree in Section 5: header, article header, related posts, footer = template-locked; body Layout Container = unlocked.

Given the body Layout Container, when an author opens it, then they can add components from the allowed list (defined in T-018) but cannot remove the container itself.

finalDraft.title: Create press-release-page proxy component over Core Page v3
finalDraft.description:
Why: The press-release template (T-004) needs a `sling:resourceType` to render. Per AEM archetype convention, proxy Core Page via `sling:resourceSuperType` rather than fork its HTL.

What: Under `ui.apps/src/main/content/jcr_root/apps/<appId>/components/page/press-release-page/` (replace `<appId>` with the archetype's configured app id, e.g. value of `${appId}` in the archetype POM), create:
- `.content.xml` — `jcr:primaryType="cq:Component"`, `componentGroup=".hidden"` (page components are hidden), `jcr:title="Press Release Page"`, `sling:resourceSuperType="core/wcm/components/page/v3/page"`. If the archetype baseline is on a newer Core Components version, update to that exact version and record the version in the commit message; do NOT use a floating reference.
- `customheaderlibs.html` — empty file with a `<!-- extended by T-003 (meta) and T-006 (clientlibs) -->` comment placeholder.
- `customfooterlibs.html` — empty file with a placeholder comment for site footer clientlibs.
- `_cq_dialog/.content.xml` — dialog inheriting Core Page dialog via `sling:resourceSuperType`, with project-specific tabs left empty here. T-002 and T-003 add their fields into this dialog.

Do NOT duplicate Core Page HTL; rely on resource super type.
acceptance_criteria: Given an author creates a press-release page from the T-004 template, when the page renders, then it inherits Core Page v3 rendering and `cq:Page` lifecycle behaviour with no HTL duplicated under the new component.

finalDraft.title: Build Article Meta HTL partial that renders releaseDate as "Published on …"
finalDraft.description:
Why: Region 3 needs a small partial that formats the typed `releaseDate` page property into the human string seen in the source ("Published on 14th April 2026 at 9:03"). Date formatting belongs in a Sling Model + HTL partial, not inline in the template.

What:
1. Add a Sling Model `com.<group>.core.models.ArticleMetaModel` under `aem-project-archetype/{ARCHETYPE_DIR}/core/src/main/java/...` that injects `releaseDate` (java.util.Calendar) from the current page and exposes `getFormattedReleaseDate()` returning `Published on Dth MMMM yyyy at H:mm` in the page's configured timezone, with ordinal day suffix (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th…11th…21st…). Use 24h time, no leading zero on hour (H:mm).
2. Add an HTL partial under `aem-project-archetype/{ARCHETYPE_DIR}/ui.apps/src/main/content/jcr_root/apps/<app>/components/content/articlemeta/articlemeta.html` that uses the model and renders a single line. Render nothing when releaseDate is missing.
3. Source the literal "Published on" and the "at" connector from the i18n bundle delivered by T-021 (key e.g. `articlemeta.publishedOn`).
4. Place the partial inside the Article Header group delivered by T-011.

Edge cases: missing `releaseDate` renders nothing (no orphan "Published on"). Ordinals must follow English rules (11th/12th/13th are 'th', not 'st/nd/rd').
acceptance_criteria: Given `releaseDate=2026-04-14T09:03:00` in the page's timezone (Australia/Sydney), when the page renders, then the meta line shows "Published on 14th April 2026 at 9:03".

Given the i18n bundle from T-021 provides the `articlemeta.publishedOn` key, when the page renders in the default locale, then the prefix "Published on" is sourced from i18n (verified by switching locale changes the prefix).
Given the partial is dropped into the Article Header group (T-011), when the page is authored, then it appears within that group and not as a standalone region.

finalDraft.title: Build custom Footnotes component with deterministic `_ftn<n>` anchor IDs
finalDraft.description:
Why: Decision #8 — source HTML has a duplicate `id="_ftnref4"` (concrete defect from RTE-anchor authoring). The Footnotes component MUST emit deterministic `id="_ftn"` anchors so inline `[n]` superscripts in body Core Text reliably target `#_ftn`. What: Create `aem-project-archetype/{ARCHETYPE_DIR}/ui.apps/.../components/content/footnotes/` with: - `.content.xml` registering the component. - `cq:dialog` with a multifield: each entry has `text` (rich-text, limited to inline formatting + links). - `footnotes.html` rendering an `
    ` (or `
    ` with numbered items) where each item carries `id="_ftn"` (1-based index, computed in HTL using the iterator) and ends with a return-arrow anchor `↩`. - A Sling Model if HTL-only iteration becomes fragile (e.g., `core/.../models/FootnotesModel.java` exposing a list of `{ index, html, refAnchorId }`). The body Core Text RTE policy (T-018) must enable anchor links so authors can hand-author `[1]` superscripts. Inline `[n]` markers in body Core Text use `#_ftnref` as the originating anchor on the marker side and `#_ftn` as the target ID on the footnote side. Edge cases: an author cannot override the anchor ID — the component computes it from list position. Re-ordering entries renumbers all anchors and breaks any inline links pointing at `#_ftn` — document this risk in the dialog help text.
acceptance_criteria: Given 4 footnote entries authored in order, when the page renders, then exactly 4 `<li id="_ftn1">…<li id="_ftn4">` (or equivalent) elements appear, each ending with a return-anchor `<a href="#_ftnref<n>">`.

Given two distinct authored pages each with 4 footnotes, when their HTML is fetched, then both render `_ftn1`–`_ftn4` deterministically with no duplicates (contrast with the source HTML's duplicate `_ftnref4`).
Given an inline `[1]` superscript in body Core Text linking to `#_ftn1`, when a user clicks it, then the browser scrolls to the first footnote entry.
Given a unit test on `FootnotesModel`, when given an empty list, then the component renders nothing (no empty `<ol>`).

finalDraft.title: Verify build, deploy, and end-to-end render of seed press-release page
finalDraft.description:
Why: Verification before completion. Once all components, templates, XFs, policies, clientlibs, content, and tests are in place, the full archetype must build and the seed page must render correctly on a local AEM SDK instance (or equivalent integration target).

What:
1. Run `mvn clean install` from `aem-project-archetype/{ARCHETYPE_DIR}/` (or the archetype's reactor root).
2. Deploy the resulting `all` package to a local AEM SDK author.
3. Open the seed page (T-022) in author and publish it.
4. Verify on publish: page renders, all six regions appear in correct order, share links open correctly, print button triggers print dialog, related-posts list populates, footnote anchors navigate correctly, page metadata is in `<head>`.
5. Run `mvn verify` to ensure JUnit tests (T-023) pass in the build.
6. Document any defects as follow-up beads issues; do NOT close until the page renders cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean local AEM SDK author, when the archetype's `all` package is deployed, then the deployment succeeds with no `OakConflict` or installation errors.
Given the seed page is published, when the published URL is fetched and inspected, then all six regions render in correct order with content matching the source.

Given an end-to-end click-through, when a user clicks Facebook share / Twitter share / Print / a footnote `[1]` superscript / a Related Posts entry, then each behaves per spec (new-tab share dialog / browser print dialog / scroll-to-anchor / navigate to listed page).
Given the build, when `mvn verify` is run, then all unit tests (T-023) pass with the coverage thresholds met.
